newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Carlton buys Rank film distribution arm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Carlton buys Rank film distribution arm.

text.p: Britain's Rank Group Plc said on Wednesday it had sold its film distribution unit, sealing its transition from a "golden era" movie-maker to a modern film services and leisure firm.
Rank sold the unit to Carlton Communications Plc for 65 million pounds ($106.9 million).

The sale completed Rank's disposal of 300 million pounds' worth of non-core assets about 10 months ahead of schedule and added classic films directed by David Lean and Alfred Hitchcock to Carlton's movie library.

"Following today's sale of Rank Film Distributors Ltd, our Film and Entertainment Services division is now clearly focused on serving the film industry, primarily the major Hollywood studios," Rank chief executive Andrew Teare said.

The deal gives Carlton a catalogue of 740 features to help feed its appetite for film and TV content, particularly after its digital broadcasting pact with Granada Group Plc and British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc.
"The demand for classic and contemporary films both in the UK and overseas is increasing all the time," Carlton chairman Michael Green said in a statement.
He added that the Rank Film library should help to ensure advertiser support for Carlton's planned film channel on digital terrestrial television.
Britain's Independent Television Commission has yet to award the licences to operate digital terrestrial TV frequencies.
The Carlton consortium faces competition from cable company International CableTel Inc.
News of the sale boosted Carlton's shares by 6.5 pence to 522.5 by 1310 GMT, while Rank's shares were up 4.5 pence to 425p.

The Rank library, which dates back to the 1930s, included titles from the British film industry's heyday, including Hitchcock's "The Lady Vanishes" and Lean's "Great Expectations", as well as recent productions like "Fried Green Tomatoes" and "The Shawshank Redemption".
Other features on the list were the classic British "Carry On" films and the Ealing comedies.
Rank, once a strong presence in British film-making, has concentrated increasingly on leisure activities such as its Hard Rock Cafe brand in the last couple of decades.
In the past eight months, Rank has sold about 11 non-core businesses as part of its disposal programme.
Rank said it would use proceeds from the sale of Rank Film Distribution to reduce debt.
Rank will remain a movie industry force through its film services business, including its renowned Pinewood Studios and its video duplication and laboratory film processing operations.
The company will also continue to own the "man with the gong" sequence that opened its films, while Carlton will have the right to use the piece on existing films in the library.
But the sale meant the final curtain for the days when Rank helped to produce films in return for the rights to distribute them later.
"It's the end of actually investing money in producing films ourselves, but we still have a huge relationship with the film industry," a Rank spokeswoman said.
Rank Film Distributors had operating profits of 4.1 million pounds in 1996. ($1=.6080 Pound)
